data.one_liner: Execute FFmpeg and FFprobe commands from Dart on Android, iOS, macOS, Windows and Linux.
data.what_it_does: Provides a single Dart API to run FFmpeg/FFprobe commands across all major platforms. Prebuilt native libraries are bundled, so no manual compilation is required.
use_when: You need to process or convert video/audio files within a Flutter app
Cross‑platform support (mobile, desktop, Linux) is required
You require hardware‑accelerated encoding/decoding on iOS/macOS
avoid_when: App size must stay minimal (the full GPL bundle is large)
Your project cannot use GPL‑licensed code
You only need a tiny subset of codecs
strengths: All major codecs including GPL ones are included
Works on Android, iOS, macOS, Windows and Linux out of the box
Prebuilt binaries mean no native build steps
weaknesses: Large binary size due to full codec set
GPL license may conflict with proprietary apps
data.setup_notes: Add the dependency and run flutter pub get. On iOS/macOS set deployment target >=15.0/11.0 in Podfile or Xcode settings; Android uses an AAR automatically.
